notes: Spent four whole turns clicking for credits at 12-20 credits with a full grip while an advanced card sat overnight in Server 1 and was scored; Afterimage went unused for most of the game.
Kept up steady R&D/HQ pressure and built a sensible rig; it ate two Urtica Ciphers, but those were reasonable runs on remotes.

Was at 6 points after a strong start, then clicked for credits for about ten straight turns up to 47 credits with a full grip, never ran the remote while agendas were advanced over several turns, and lost.
Good R&D pressure with Carmen and a clean final steal; the run on a known Nico Campaign remote through two unrezzed ice was low value.

Drifted for many turns, rich and making few runs, while the Corp discarded agendas to Archives each turn; it jacked out after bypassing Starlit Knight, reinstalled a unique Docklands Pass, and paid 9 to save minor hardware.

Ran Server 1 three or four times a turn, over and over, into an unbroken Ansel 1.0 whose sub stops any steal, so every run was pointless while the Corp scored those same agendas; it never installed a breaker that could answer Ansel.
Simple but effective R&D pressure through Funhouse, taking tags rather than paying; some clicks went to tag removal and redundant draws.
Clicked for credits nearly every turn up to 65 credits, never played its five-card grip or found breakers, and let the Corp score agendas advanced over several turns.
Sat on 20-45 credits clicking for credits while the Corp advanced agendas overnight and left naked remotes; it made only one real remote run and jacked out of it.
Sensible remote and HQ pressure with Rising Tide; economy was tight, but it took the winning steals when they opened up.
Trashed its only breaker to Spec Work early and spent much of the game near 0 credits; persistent R&D runs eventually won, but drawing over hand size and rare HQ runs were sloppy.
Built a large economy (20-31 credits) but never got a barrier answer or contested Server 1, where agendas sat advanced overnight and were scored for the win.
Clicked for credits for six-plus turns up to 39 credits while Next Big Thing and Tomorrow's Headline were advanced across turns in Server 1, without ever running it again.
Against a net-damage Corp that had already hit for 2, it facechecked unrezzed HQ ice with a 3-card grip on its last click and was flatlined by Saisentan.
Efficient aggressive play across HQ, R&D and the remotes, with good use of Shibboleth and Revolver; it ran low on credits late but closed out the game.
Ran R&D three or four times a turn, which mostly re-saw the same top card; it never installed breakers and so could not contest the Hagen remote where agendas were scored.
Stalled mid-game on repeated Archives runs and tag cleanup while the Corp sat broke; once Banner landed it pressured HQ and R&D well and won.
Spent turn 1 on repeat R&D runs instead of hitting the naked remote agenda, then clicked for credits up to 37 while the Corp scored out of remotes.
Generally good remote pressure, but it reached the second Méliès City Luxury Line with no click left to pay its steal cost and the Corp scored it next turn.
Wouldn't pay 3 credits to get through Grubber while sitting on 23, then clicked for credits up to 42 as the Corp advanced and scored three agendas in that server.
